transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I'm having some trouble with how I look. 

The left side of my face is just really uneven and puffy. I can't stop focusing on it, especially during video calls for work, or... in photos from my salsa class. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see what I'm talking about, but... I do. And it's just kind of... getting to the point where it's messing with my job and my social life, I guess.
Is it just your face that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you worry are uneven or flawed?
Um... no. Just my face, really. I haven't... I don't really notice anything else. Just that one side.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to fix or check your face?

Um... yeah, I guess I do. Before my meetings, or... if I'm supposed to go somewhere, I'll open the camera preview on my computer. I just end up... changing the angle and the lighting a lot. And fixing my hair around that side of my face to see if it helps. 

Sometimes I take a bunch of pictures, or... I'll ask my friends if I look strange. I just keep doing it until I'm late. Or... sometimes I just get too drained to even go out at all.
Do you have any thoughts or mental images that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't think I do that. It's just the checking things I mentioned.
Do you feel like your concerns about your face are causing you a lot of distress?

Um... yeah. I guess it is. I've... I've missed some ticket deadlines at work because of it. And... I've been late to a few video calls. My supervisor actually brought it up during my last performance review. 

And... outside of work, I don't know. I guess I've skipped some things. Like salsa nights, or... community events. Especially if I know people are going to be taking pictures. I just... I can't do it.
Do you think something bad would happen if you didn't check your face like you do?
Um... no. Not like... a specific bad thing happening. I just... I feel like I have to do it. It's just really uncomfortable if I don't.
Do you have any habits or rituals that you feel you must do every day?

Um... well, mostly just the camera stuff. Like... before a work meeting, or if I'm supposed to go somewhere. I just... I keep opening the camera preview. I have to change the angles and the lighting, and... I keep fixing my hair around that side of my face. 

Sometimes I retake pictures over and over, or... I'll ask my friends if I look strange. I just kind of get stuck doing it until... well, until I'm late. Or until I'm just too drained to even go out.
Do you feel like the left side of your face needs to be perfectly symmetrical with the right side?
Um... I don't know if it's about being perfect. I just... I don't want it to look the way it does. It just bothers me.
Do you think your face would be okay if the left and right sides were not exactly the same, but still looked good in their own way?
I... I don't know. I guess I just... I can't really picture that. It just... it doesn't look right to me.
Do you ever have thoughts about your face that repeat in your mind even when you're not actively trying to check or fix it?
Um... I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really noticed if they repeat like that. I guess it's just... always kind of on my mind. But I'm not really sure.
Do you think you would still be bothered by your face if someone you trusted told you that it looked fine and that the asymmetry was not noticeable?

Um... well, people actually already do that. They keep telling me they don't see anything. But... it doesn't really help. I just... I can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side looks. Especially when I have to be on video calls for work... or in photos from my salsa class. It's just... it's starting to really mess with my job and my social life, even when they say it's fine.
Do you feel like checking your face is something you can control, or is it something that you feel compelled to do?

I... I guess it's hard to stop. It feels like I just have to do it. Like, before a meeting or... or going out, I'll open the camera preview. And then I just get stuck. I keep changing the angle, or the lighting... messing with my hair to try and hide that side. I'll retake pictures over and over, or ask my friends if I look weird. I don't really want to, but... I just keep doing it until I'm late. Or until I'm just too drained to even go anywhere.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check your face if you weren't worried about how it looks?
Um... I don't know. I guess... probably not? I mean, if I wasn't worried about it, I wouldn't need to look. But... I just am worried about it.
Do you think you would still check your face as frequently if you were alone and didn't have to interact with anyone?
Um... I guess so. I mean... I still do it when I'm by myself. It's not just about other people... I just... I still see it.
Do you think the thoughts about your face are what drive you to check it, or is it the other way around, that checking your face makes you think about it more?
I... I don't really know. I guess... maybe both? I just... the thoughts are always there, and then I look, and... it just makes it worse, I guess. I'm not really sure which starts it.
Do you feel like you would still feel anxious or uncomfortable if you didn't check your face, even if you weren't thinking about how it looks?
I'm... not sure. I mean, if I wasn't thinking about it, maybe I wouldn't be anxious? But... I don't really know how to separate the two. It's hard to imagine not thinking about it.
Do you think you would still feel the urge to check your face if you couldn't change your appearance or fix what you see as the problem?

I... I think I still would. Even if I can't fix it, I just... I have to look. Like, before I have to get on a video call for work, or if I'm supposed to go somewhere... I'll just sit there opening the camera preview on my phone or computer. I keep tilting my head, trying to find an angle or different lighting where it doesn't look as bad... pulling my hair over that side of my face to hide it. I'll take pictures over and over, and... sometimes I text them to my friends, asking if it looks weird. I just keep doing it until... I'm usually late, or I just feel so exhausted from it that I don't even want to go out anymore. So... yeah, I guess the urge is just always there, even if I can't actually change anything.
Do you think you would feel better about your face if the left and right sides were more symmetrical, even if they weren't perfectly even?

I don't know... maybe? I just... the whole reason I'm here is because I can't stop focusing on it. It just looks so uneven and puffy on the left side, especially on my work video calls... or in photos from my salsa class. People keep telling me they don't see it, but... I do. And it's just... it's really starting to mess with my job and... everything else. I just want it to not look like that.
Do you think the discomfort you feel is more because of how your face looks or because you feel like you have to check it?
I'm not really sure. Um... I guess I don't really know which is worse. It just... it all just feels bad. I don't really know how to separate them.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check your face if you were completely alone and had no intention of interacting with anyone or being seen by them?
I... I don't really know. Um... I guess I haven't really thought about it. I'm just not sure if I would or not.
